title: Four Ways to Remember
description: A Bloom filter, a skip list, union-find and cuckoo hashing — four data structures most courses never reach, each built to answer one question fast, and each shown storing real data one operation at a time.
long_description:
Every structure here answers a single question, and the wall shows how it is actually stored while it does.

The Bloom filter asks have I seen this before? It never stores what you put into it — only 32 bits — so it can tell you definitely not with certainty and probably otherwise. Watch a name it was never given come back as a yes.

The skip list asks what comes next? It is a sorted linked list with express lanes built over it, and a coin flip decides which values get one. No rotations, no rebalancing, and still O(log n).

Union-find asks are these two connected? It is an array of integers, nothing more. Watch a four-deep chain collapse flat in a single pass of path compression.

Cuckoo hashing asks where did I put it? Every key has exactly two slots it may use, so a lookup is always two probes — but an insert can shove a key out, which shoves out another, and past about half full the whole thing has to be rebuilt.

None of it is staged: the hash functions are real, and the false positive and the eviction cycle are found by running the algorithm, not drawn in.
action_hints: pick one of the four structures to stay on
slow it down to follow an operation
pause on the part you want to read
deal new data and watch it play out differently
